one_liner: Open-source WordPress plugin for building and managing online stores.

evidence.claim: Authentication uses consumer key/consumer secret pairs passed via HTTP basic auth
evidence.quote: For Authorization, choose **basic auth** and enter your **consumer key** and **consumer secret** keys from WooCommerce into the username and password fields.

evidence.claim: API keys are self-generated by any store user from the WordPress admin at no cost
evidence.quote: To create or manage keys for a specific WordPress user, go to WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API.

evidence.claim: Full CRUD REST API over JSON, integrated with the WordPress REST API (v3)
evidence.quote: This allows WC data to be created, read, updated, and deleted using requests in JSON format and using WordPress REST API Authentication methods

evidence.claim: v3 API surface is broad, spanning dozens of resource APIs (orders, products, customers, coupons, taxes, shipping, settings, webhooks, etc.)
evidence.quote: By default, the API provides information about all available endpoints on the site. Authentication is not required to access the API index.

evidence.claim: WooCommerce officially ships/documents an MCP integration on its own docs site
evidence.quote: MCP for WooCommerce connects Claude, ChatGPT, and other AI assistants to your WooCommerce store so they can work with your orders, products, customers, and more

notes: WooCommerce 10.9+ is agent-ready with a native MCP endpoint at /wp-json/woocommerce/mcp, documented at developer.woocommerce.com/docs/features/mcp/. Because WooCommerce is self-hosted, credentials (ck_/cs_ keys) are per-store; an Application Authentication Endpoint (/wc-auth/v1/authorize) lets third-party apps auto-generate keys via a redirect flow (OAuth-like, not true OAuth2). Official SDKs exist for JS, PHP, Python, Ruby. Any WP REST API auth plugin/method also works. Requires pretty permalinks enabled.
